title: GONG MODEL -- physical-model gong, from harmonic string to tam-tam

sections.heading: USING IT
lines: Turn on audio with the speaker button (top right). Pick a sound from the preset menu.
Play MIDI notes: note = pitch, velocity = strike force, aftertouch = hand damping.
Or click test strike: the upper number is its pitch (Hz), vel: is its strike force (0-1).
random: sets every dial to a random value (output gain excepted).
Tone: Structure morphs harmonic > gamelan > nipple gong > church bell > tam-tam.
Brightness, Decay, Nonlinearity; Material picks wool, felt, rubber, wood or metal mallet.
Exciter: Hardness, Vel Curve, Audio In (feeds live input into the gong).
Strike XY: where on the gong surface the mallet hits.
Bloom: Bloom, Bloom Speed, Bloom Persist -- the slow swell of high partials after a hard strike.
Output: Gain, Noise Level, Stereo Width, Modes (8-32 resonators), Detune.
Mode Spectrum: draw the level of each mode.
Drift: toggle On/Off to let the dials wander around their current positions.
Enable / Range / Rate set each dial's drift; Speed (ms) sets the update rate.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: gen~ gong-engine is a bank of up to 32 resonators whose tuning morphs between five ratio tables.
A mallet model excites them; nonlinear coupling passes energy from low to high modes (bloom).
It is one voice: a new strike damps and re-excites the modes that are still ringing.
Dials reach gen~ through send gong-ctrl; js scripts handle mode gains, randomize and drift.
